emerging_technology: Generative AI, including large language models and retrieval-supported research and drafting capabilities.
intended_application: Create optional first drafts of internal ecommerce listing copy and tags from approved structured catalog attributes. Merchandisers edit and approve drafts before publication.
organization: Hypothetical small domestic online retailer with a lean merchandising team and seasonal catalog changes.
industry_sector: Domestic ecommerce catalog operations in a single working language.
business_need: Reduce repetitive editing and speed up listing preparation while preserving factual product attributes and consistent wording.
users_stakeholders: Merchandisers, catalog operations, the ecommerce platform owner, and shoppers downstream.
adoption_posture: Early experimenter for bounded, reversible internal workflows.
capabilities_constraints: Assume a structured catalog and deterministic templates are available, customer information is excluded, and existing editorial approval can be retained. Budget, export compatibility, and time savings are unverified.
risk_consequence_context: Invented attributes, unsupported product claims, inconsistent tags, and platform lock-in could cause rework or mislead shoppers if missed at review. Drafts can be discarded before publication.
management_question: Should the retailer run a four-week sandbox using a platform-native feature or a standalone model, and under what conditions should it prefer templates or switch tools?
time_horizon: Four weeks to compare tools against the current template baseline before the next catalog update.
